articles.excerpt: A free-text failure message can contain more structure than its format suggests. Semicolons separate observations, recurring phrases identify criteria, and numbers describe the measured values. Extrac…
articles.body: A free-text failure message can contain more structure than its format suggests. Semicolons separate observations, recurring phrases identify criteria, and numbers describe the measured values. Extracting that structure makes it possible to distinguish a failed record from the several reasons attached to it. The published benchmark links its broader records through the downloadable results . For this exercise, the working input is framing_reasons.csv , a flat export with the columns tool , room , framing_pass and framing . Decide what the counter measures Count recorded reasons rather than attempting to reconstruct the underlying measurements. That distinction matters because the messages contain displayed values, which may not preserve the precision used for the original judgment.

articles.title: MongoDB to BigQuery Without Datastream or Kafka: A Change Stream CDC Tutorial
articles.excerpt: BigQuery wants columns, and MongoDB hands you documents that get rewritten in place. A MongoDB to BigQuery pipeline has to close both gaps: turn fields into columns, and carry every update and delete…
articles.body: BigQuery wants columns, and MongoDB hands you documents that get rewritten in place. A MongoDB to BigQuery pipeline has to close both gaps: turn fields into columns, and carry every update and delete across instead of shipping yesterday's export. The common ways to move the data: mongoexport to JSON, then bq load . A script, a scheduler and a staging bucket. Freshness is hours to daily, and every run is a full reload, so updates and deletes never arrive as changes. Datastream for MongoDB . Google's managed service reads change streams into native BigQuery datasets, near real time by Google's description. There is nothing to run, and BigQuery is the only reader of the result. Debezium, Kafka and a BigQuery sink.

articles.body: Most release checklists I have seen stop at "tests are green and someone clicked through staging". That someone almost always clicks through in English, with a mouse, on a laptop. Then the German build ships with a checkout button that reads "Zur Kas", and a screen reader user hears "button, button, button" on the payment step. This is the checklist we use before a release. None of it needs a specific tool. I will mention what we built at the end, but everything here works with Playwright, axe-core and an afternoon. 1. Test the real build, not the translation files Linting your .json locale files catches missing keys. It does not catch what users actually see: Clipped text. German, Finnish and Russian strings are often 30 to 40 percent longer than English.

articles.title: Turning Singlish into Sinhala Unicode with a longest-match token table
articles.excerpt: Sinhala is an abugida. A consonant letter carries an inherent vowel, vowels written after a consonant are signs that attach to it, and a special mark kills the inherent vowel. Typing it from a Latin k…
articles.body: Sinhala is an abugida. A consonant letter carries an inherent vowel, vowels written after a consonant are signs that attach to it, and a special mark kills the inherent vowel. Typing it from a Latin keyboard ("Singlish") means turning ammaa into අම්මා. I wrote a converter for this as part of Singlish to Sinhala , and the interesting part is how little machinery it needs: one map, a longest-match scan, and a couple of flags of state. This post walks through that design. Nothing here depends on the site; the same approach works for other abugidas. The token table There are two tables: 16 vowels and 44 consonant keys.

articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. articles.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
articles.excerpt: These strange geological features may offer clues to the Red Planet's watery past.
articles.body: NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life.

articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The NASA+ original documentary “The Europa Concept” takes audiences along on the journey to send a spacecraft to Jupiter’s moon Europa to determine whether the ocean beneath the moon’s icy shell has the ingredients for life.  Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech NASA invites the world behind the scenes to witness the story of Europa Clipper’s journey from a far-off vision to a cutting-edge deep space exploration mission with the release of the agency’s newest documentary, “The Europa Concept.” The documentary will air on NASA+ , the NASA app, and the agency’s website starting Monday, Nov. 23, and is coming soon to YouTube.
